ratings.why: Ordinary @Scribe mentions vary by position and nearby punctuation, so a careful builder pins one stable contains-rule and tests it, while case folding and email-like strings are a smaller mismatch.
Most room traffic is ordinary talk, and dropping those lines or calling POST /api/agent for them breaks the conversation the operator is reading.
Shift+Enter is how a multiline draft is written, and sending on that keystroke posts text Maya had not finished.
Mentioning Scribe is how Maya gets an answer, and a reply that is missing, mistyped, or not the returned text leaves the operator with nothing to read.
If a network error, HTTP error, or unusable body is not a failure, the working state stays up and Retry Scribe never appears.
Maya needs a clear in-page failure that clears on success, and a blocking dialog or a Retry left on the wrong message is a real but secondary trap.
Retry means the failed reply again, and posting the current draft or a later message answers text Maya did not send for that line.
A sluggish Send or Retry invites a second activation, and an extra person line or a second Scribe reply is worth preventing even though a deliberate second send is still a real message.
A careful builder either keeps the composer usable and attaches each reply to its own message, or says that a second send waits, because a swapped reply confuses the thread.
The role=status cue is what a waiting person has, and a status that never appears, or stays after the reply or the failure alert, contradicts the outcome on screen.
Enter on a blank or newline-only draft is a normal slip, and the composer and the HTTP 400 have to share one whitespace set so nothing is added and a blank body is rejected.
The request only says whitespace-only text is ignored, so an enabled Send button that leaves a blank draft in place is a reasonable behavior.
The Demo reply echoes the sent text, so a careful builder keeps one version of leading, trailing, and internal whitespace across the bubble, the POST body, and the echo.
The built-in page sends well-formed JSON, but a maintainer calling the endpoint by hand needs a client error for a bad body and a process that stays up.
Success has to be the stated JSON text and whitespace has to be HTTP 400, and a stable content type plus a parseable 400 body keep the page and the tests from misreading them.
The delivery only needs GET / and POST /api/agent, so a default answer for PUT or /nope is enough and a method matrix is extra.
A hand-rolled static handler can expose server.js, tests, or files outside the project to anyone who can open the port, which a careful builder closes.
The request says a local app listens on PORT, and the default bind is a reasonable choice for a one-room demo with no accounts.
A taken or invalid port already fails at startup through Node, and a custom message is polish this delivery can skip.
Person lines and the Scribe echo are message text, and interpreting angle brackets as HTML drops what Maya typed and can run it.
A navigation or reload on send discards a session-only transcript, brings the seed back, and drops an in-flight agent call.
Session storage is allowed, and the operator and the maintainer need a stated choice for what a reload, a new tab, or a second tab keeps.
/?empty=1 must open an empty sendable room, and stored messages overriding it or the fixture wiping Launch plan make both URLs wrong.
The empty start should say how to write and how to call Scribe, and that note should go away once a message is actually in the room.
The control is specified to start as Use dark appearance, so the room has to open in the light appearance or the label is wrong.
Use light appearance has to bring back the light room and the Use dark appearance label, including on later toggles of the same control.
The appearance button has to stay visible and usable at 320px, 390px, and 1440px, or the required control and the required widths both fail.
Dark appearance still needs readable messages, times, badges, the failure alert, and a visible focus indicator, or the theme switch is hard to use.
Pasted URLs and long unbroken tokens are common in a project room and are the usual reason a layout that fits short lines starts scrolling sideways at the required widths.
A short seeded room still works if Maya scrolls to a new line herself, so auto-scroll is a convenience a simple page can omit.
Maya can click the Message box again after sending, and returning focus there is a typing convenience the request does not depend on.
A screen-reader user already hears the working status, and a live announcement of the new Scribe reply is the careful way for them to learn that the answer arrived.
Shown times need a believable order and a stable format so the seed does not read as broken and the maintainer can test them.
The operator reads the Launch plan seed first, and a new message that lands in the wrong place makes the thread unreadable.
Nothing in the request caps message or body size, and an uncapped local demo is a reasonable build.
Enter and Shift+Enter are the stated keys, and IME composition plus the phone keyboard's newline are platform edges this delivery can leave alone.
The next maintainer has to run the required suite with node --test, and that depends on a Node version whose node:test discovery matches the command.
Scribe is supposed to be a clearly identified demonstration agent, and a visible agent identity on its articles is what keeps it distinct from Maya and Theo in a demo.
The customer demos the seeded Launch plan, so the lines should read as a coherent conversation, with the exact wording left as a writing choice.
The current user is Maya and there are no accounts, so composer messages have to be hers and there is no control to post as Theo.
